subject: Repricing for Q3 capacity uplift & temporary price hold
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@brightmart.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@brightmart.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity uplift for Q3 + request for temporary rate hold

Hi Naomi,

Hope you’re well — BrightMart is projecting a material uptick in query volume for our recommendation pipelines starting mid-July through September (holiday prep + new campaign). We’re evaluating a staged capacity uplift: +40% in July, +65% in August, +30% in September (compared to current committed baseline).

Before we run internal procurement, two asks: 1) can Redwood provide a temporary price hold for the uplifted units (so we don’t get variable price spikes while onboarding the extra capacity), and 2) are there one-time onboarding or seat credits you can apply to offset the migration work?

If you need numbers, I attached the PO template and a quick forecast. We’d like to close terms and issue a PO by the second week of May if possible.

Attachment: BrightMart_PO_Template.pdf (pdf)

Thanks —
Elena Rossi
Head of Data Platforms, BrightMart
elena@brightmart.com
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@brightmart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity uplift for Q3 + request for temporary rate hold

On Tue, May 4, 2027 at 9:12 AM Elena Rossi <elena@brightmart.com> wrote:
> Hi Naomi,
>
> Hope you’re well — BrightMart is projecting a material uptick in query volume for our recommendation pipelines starting mid-July through September...

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads up and the forecast. We can definitely design a short-term protection for the uplift while you stabilize the routing and prefixes. High-level proposal (internal shortform):

- Temporary price hold: Hold rates for uplifted units for an initial 3-month window covering July–September.
- Staged uplift credits: Prorated onboarding credit applied against first invoice of uplift (tiered by month; example term sheet attached).
- SLA credit bucket: If latency/availability degrades beyond agreed SLOs during the uplift, a pre-funded SLA credit pool reduces your financial exposure.

I’ve attached a draft term sheet (Redwood_Staged_Uplift_Term_Sheet_v1.pdf) with a sample math example. Can you confirm the absolute uplift units (TPU-hours or token units) and whether BrightMart needs a hard cap on overage fees?

We’ll loop legal/finance if you want the draft as an order form amendment and a DocuSign ready flow.

Attachment: Redwood_Staged_Uplift_Term_Sheet_v1.pdf (pdf)

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
From: Elena Rossi <elena@brightmart.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@brightmart.com>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity uplift for Q3 + request for temporary rate hold

Thanks Naomi — attaching the forecast spreadsheet with month-by-month expected token consumption and provisional CPU/GPU-hour estimates.

A couple clarifications:
- We want a hard cap on overage exposure during the initial 90 days (BrightMart cannot take more than +80% over baseline without prior written sign-off). If usage exceeds the cap, we’ll pay pre-agreed overage rates only after a manual sign-off.
- Onboarding credits: would prefer a one-time credit applied to July invoice.
- Procurement wants a 6-month rate hold if possible rather than 3 months to cover any lag in usage stabilization.

Attachment: brightmart_forecast_q3.xlsx (xls)

cc: Tom Brice (CFO) to keep him in the loop.

—Elena
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: pricing math and concession request (brightmart)

Marissa / Naomi — internal calc and recommendation below (do not forward externally without approval):

Summary: BrightMart asks for a 6-month price hold + hard overage cap + onboarding credit. Arena: this is mid-size enterprise account; incremental MRR from uplift estimated at ~$60k/month at list.

Proposed concession profile:
- Price hold: 6 months on uplifted units (per Elena request).
- Discount on committed uplift: 8% off list for the uplift tranche (months where they are above baseline and below hard cap).
- One-time onboarding credit: $25,000 applied to first invoice of uplift.
- SLA credit pool: $15,000 pre-funded credit that offsets objective SLA misses during uplift window.

Concession cost estimate (run-rate impact across 6 months): ~$85k-$110k total. Any concession > $50k requires Sales VP approval per comp/discount matrix. Recommend we ask Marissa to sign off and route to VP Sales for the delta.

If approved, we prepare an amendment + order form and a PO-ready DocuSign packet. Also advise ops to reserve an extra capacity buffer in our Dedicated pool for the July–Aug window.

—David
Head of Renewals Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@brightmart.com>, Procurement <procurement@brightmart.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity uplift for Q3 + request for temporary rate hold

Hi Elena / Procurement — thanks for the forecast and the cap request. We’ve reviewed internally and can move forward with a counter proposal to cover both stabilization and procurement timelines. Key points: 

1) Price hold: 6 months (Jul–Dec) specifically on uplifted units — rates held at current committed price for the uplift tranche.
2) Discount: 8% on uplifted committed units (applied month-to-month while usage is above baseline and below the 80% cap).
3) Onboarding credit: one-time $25,000 credit applied to July invoice.
4) SLA credit pool: $15,000; definition and triggers attached (SLA_Credit_Definition.xlsx).
5) Hard cap on unapproved overage: 80% over baseline; any consumption beyond that requires written sign-off from BrightMart procurement.
6) DocuSign / PO: We’ll prepare an amendment and order form; DocuSign link below. Please review and confirm so Procurement can issue the PO.

DocuSign (amendment & order form): https://www.docusign.net/BRM-2027-041
Attachment: SLA_Credit_Definition.xlsx (xlsx)

If that works, Naomi will follow up with the exact amended order form and revised invoice schedule (we can prorate July if the uplift starts mid-month).

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Sales Manager, Enterprise Renewals
Redwood Inference
From: Elena Rossi <elena@brightmart.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@brightmart.com>, Tom Brice <t.brice@brightmart.com>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity uplift for Q3 + request for temporary rate hold

Marissa / Naomi — thank you. BrightMart accepts the counter: 6-month price hold, 8% uplift discount, $25k onboarding credit, $15k SLA credit pool, 80% hard cap on overage. We will issue the PO today and attach our signed PO.

Attachment: Signed_PO_BrightMart_2027-05-07.pdf (pdf)

Next steps we need from Redwood:
- Updated order form / amendment for signature (DocuSign link to be returned to us before EOD Monday)
- Revised invoice schedule showing prorated July charges and the onboarding credit line item
- Ops confirmation of capacity reservation for July–August (contact: ops-oncall@redwood.ai)

Tom Brice (CFO) signing — tl;dr: we appreciate the speed here.

Best,
Elena Rossi
Head of Data Platforms, BrightMart
elena@brightmart.com
